sections.name: II. 'The Name Is WAWALUGI': The Blacked-Out Line and the Leaking Vault
sections.imageCaption: Mr. T asleep across the Archive Hall desk beside the open red-stained grimoire and the scored sheet while water drips from the uncracked vault overhead and Waluigi leaves into the rain.
sections.overview:
Mr. T stopped him at the doorway with the obvious question: **"Wario already IS Bowser for most games? What do you mean by that?"**

Waluigi turned with one hand still on the frame, walked back, and dropped into his chair like a man deflating. **"Look at it logically! Mario and Luigi are brothers. Wario is their cousin. He's ALREADY the rival version of Mario. Do they really think just because he has a Koopa shell that makes him an entirely different franchise?! And then there's me — the one who gets left out! The 'W' in Waluigi is RIGHT THERE, people are supposed to see it, but nooo—"**

He held his working notebook up like a shield. Mr. T tilted his head: **"I thought it was like Wa Wario and Wa Wa Luigi, no? The evil-evil version of you two."**

Waluigi's eye twitched. **"Wa Wario?"** He said the words like sour milk. **"And Wa Luigi? Don't you DARE get those two names confused with mine! I'm Waluigi. Singular. Unique. The only one of my kind in existence!"**

**"No, no,"** Mr. T corrected calmly. **"Wawaluigi. Two Wa's."**

All the color drained out of Waluigi's face. His mouth opened twice before any sound came out: **"W-Wawal... ugi?"** His chair tipped back hard enough to nearly throw him. **"Do they seriously have a Wa Waluigi character? And they put him right next to me?! To Wario?!"** His pen flew across the Archive Hall, missed the target wall by several feet, and hit the plaster with a dull *thunk*. He buried his face in both hands over the fluttering pages of his grimoire and whispered it to the wood: **"Wawalugi... The name is WAWALUGI. WA WALUGI!"**

**"I guess you want to scrap this, then,"** Mr. T said.

At the word *scrap*, Waluigi's head snapped up. Slowly he retrieved his pen — nib still wet with ledger ink — and drove a hard, jagged black line straight through **'Waluigi'** on the sheet until nothing white showed underneath. **"Scrap this whole mess. No more confusion. No more evil versions. This isn't about the Wa characters. This is about ME. And if anyone else thinks they can just erase me like this again..."**

He stood, pulled his rain-damp cloak across his shoulders, and walked for the door. **"I need to clear my head. Get out of here."** Halfway across the threshold he glanced back for one flickered beat, muttered **"Don't wait up,"** and clicked the door shut behind him.

Alone in the quiet hall, Mr. T read back over his own notes — Waluigi's clenched jaw, the six names, the half-finished line where he had stopped himself — and saw a drop slide down the glass. Looking ten feet straight up into the vaulted stone ceiling, he murmured, **"Is the ceiling leaking?"** A fresh dark stain was spreading across uncracked stone, dropping irregular beads of water onto the flags: *pitter-patter... pitter-patter...* Thinking to himself that it sounded *like music*, Mr. T lowered his head into his hands beside the open red-stained grimoire and fell asleep.

*WAH! Yes, I threw the pen, and yes, it missed by four feet — the nib was weighted wrong and my cheekbone was already throbbing from twenty-four hours earlier! Try hearing somebody calmly explain that there is now a 'Wawaluigi' with two Wa's while your real notebook is sitting in a stranger's satchel and tell me you keep your pen on the blotter!*
sections.waluigi_note: Note the fresh water stain directly above the table. No crack in the stone, dry when I walked out, dripping within minutes. Remember that when Wario starts complaining about the building.

sections.name: III. 'Wake Up, Sleepyhead': Wario, the Brass Key, and Ten Thousand Missing Gold
sections.overview:
Measured footsteps crossed the cold stone while Mr. T slept — circling the table once in the dark, stopping directly behind his chair, waiting through two steady drips from the vault overhead. Something cool touched the back of his neck, then tapped his shoulder a second time right beside his ear:

**"Wake up, sleepyhead."**

Mr. T raised his head with a groggy **"Uggu"** to find **Wario** leaning beside the chair, his red cap sitting slightly askew, golden eyes glinting above a crooked grin. **"Ugh? Really? After all that groaning and complaining about being tired..."** Wario clapped the back of his head roughly, glanced with open disgust at the scattered inventory sheets — **"useless busywork if I ever saw it"** — and when Mr. T stared back blankly without moving, jabbed both thumbs at his own chest.

**"I am Wario! The Explosive Accountant! And you're just... what exactly are you supposed to be?"**

Mr. T pushed himself out of the chair. **"Alright... what is on the agenda?"**

Wario's whole posture snapped straight to business. From the inside pocket of his coat he pulled a thick sheaf of financial schedules that Waluigi had sent over that morning. **"The numbers don't add up. Not even close. I've been checking my own grimoire against these figures for three hours now, and I can tell you right now — this is either a mistake or someone's trying to pull some kind of fast one over on us."**

Stepping shoulder to shoulder with Mr. T, Wario dragged one gloved finger down [[prop:prop_warios_enterprise_ledger_discrepancy|the open ledger columns]]:

**"Look here — column seven versus column nine. See how they're different by almost ten thousand gold? That's not accounting error; that's fraud or incompetence. Either Waluigi's been cooking books again and hasn't told us about it, or someone else is playing games with our ledgers."** He flipped hard to a quarterly client deposit and tapped the timestamp. **"This was logged almost two weeks before any actual business transaction would have occurred that makes sense."**

When Mr. T asked who stood to gain by faking them, Wario lowered his voice — **"this isn't just about money anymore — this is politics"** — and produced a **small brass key** from his coat pocket, admitting he had already used it on locked filing cabinets earlier and found *"interesting things."* Mr. T asked flatly whether Waluigi owed him coin. Wario looked away toward the rain-streaked glass before his jaw set: **"We're family... He owes me money. Big time. And then he has the audacity to send me paperwork that might be fake?"**
sections.waluigi_note: 'The Explosive Accountant.' He gave himself that title at full volume in an empty vault while holding a brass key to cabinets he swears nobody can get into. Keep count of how many things Wario calls impossible right before doing them himself.

sections.name: IV. The Shelf Backups, the Treasury of Wonders, and 'AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO'
sections.imageCaption: Wario slams open *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* beside his brass cabinet key as Mr. T points to 'AUDIT REQUIRED' in the bottom-left corner and a bruised Waluigi comes through the glass door clutching a scorched notebook.
sections.overview:
Mr. T glanced past Wario's shoulder toward the entrance — where **Waluigi** was standing directly behind the Archive Hall door with his ears pressed flat against the glass.

The door swung open and Waluigi strode in rumpled and furious, a fresh bruise darkening his cheekbone and **a badly scorched notebook** clutched tight against his chest. **"I got here about twenty minutes ago,"** he snapped when Wario moved closer to check his face. **"I was just dealing with some... complications. That's none of your concern right now. What matters is that I'm here and we can finally start figuring out what the hell is going on with these fake ledgers."** Outside in the distant hallway, running boots and urgent voices briefly shouted something about an emergency before fading.

While the two of them bristled over who in the kingdom wanted Waluigi ruined, Mr. T turned to the oak shelves, pulled a bound volume down at random, and held its cover up to Wario.

Wario froze, then lunged forward to snatch it out of his hands. **"You've got to be kidding me — *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise*... this is actually the real thing!"** Seconds later Mr. T pulled down a second volume beside it; Wario pried that one free too, stacking both authentic backup ledgers together. **"Public? You think THIS Archive Hall is just some public library where anyone can wander in off the street?! This place houses the most sensitive financial records in all of civilization! There are supposed to be guards on duty at all times!"**

Mr. T looked across at Waluigi: **"When you first brought me in here, I don't remember there being anyone on guard."**

**"I— I didn't either,"** Waluigi admitted quietly, tugging at his coat collar. **"I've been coming here for months now, and I always assumed there would be someone watching. Turns out that trust was misplaced."**

Wario's trembling fingers raced down the genuine backup columns until his palm slammed flat on the page: **"There! That's not right! This transaction here... it shows that I withdrew 5,000 gold coins from the Treasury of Wonders three months ago. But according to these records, those same funds should have been deposited into my account exactly one month after that date! Someone's been cooking the books!"**

At the words *Treasury of Wonders*, Mr. T asked whether the Toads controlled it — and joked straight-faced: **"Yeah, this is definitely fraud. Should I contact the TPF — Toad Police Force?"**

Both men went rigid at once. **"WAIT!"** Wario barked, going pale under his tan. **"Do NOT contact them! Do not tell a single soul about this!"**

**"It was a joke, calm down,"** Mr. T said dryly. **"I should know — I am the one who cleans the dirty laundry. In fact, I told you about it a few months ago in your daily reports, Wario. Let's pull out the paper with the discrepancy and check the bottom."**

They turned the sheet over to its bottom-left corner. Jabbed into the margin in tiny, unmistakable ink sat four words:

> **`AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO`**

**"Of COURSE you told me. I'm a fool,"** Wario groaned, dragging both hands down his face. **"This changes everything."**

*WAH! Months! MONTHS! Mr. T wrote WARIO'S OWN NAME after a hyphen at the bottom of the exact discrepancy page, filed it in the daily packet, and 'The Explosive Accountant' filed it straight into oblivion while lecturing the rest of us about competence! Frame that margin corner in gold!*
sections.waluigi_note: Read the sequence carefully: genuine backups sitting openly on unguarded shelves, forged morning schedules swapped into circulation, and a 5,000-gold Treasury of Wonders loop sitting unread under Wario's own thumb.

sections.name: V. The Third Haunting This Week: Footsteps in the Clinic and the Crushed Flower
sections.imageCaption: Beta Luigi drives his heavy boot through a live Fire Flower on the wet Archive Hall stones as lightning breaks outside and pale phantoms coil around the door; Wario and Waluigi watch from between the stacks.
sections.overview:
Before anyone could turn another page, muffled footsteps broke the silence from the connected clinic hallways — multiple sets of boots moving fast where nobody belonged at that hour.

**"Shit,"** Waluigi whispered, tucking the ledger tight under one arm and backing into the shadow of the stacks. **"The hallways are supposed to be empty this time of—"** A distant door slammed open, followed by raised voices. Wario clapped one hand over his coat pocket — right over the hidden **Contract of Accord** — pulled Mr. T down into deep cover between two massive oak bookcases, and breathed directly into his ear: **"Stay completely silent. If we move even an inch, they'll hear us."**

The Archive Hall door creaked slowly inward.

Work boots scraped across the floorboards. Out from behind the stacks stepped **Beta Luigi** — dressed in stained green overalls with a heavy leather tool belt pulled high over one shoulder, his dark green cap tugged low enough to swallow his upper face.

Phantoms materialized around him in the doorway and sang together as thunder cracked outside the windows:

> *Fell up high to rock bottom, the guilt in your stomach feels uneasy —*  
> *now he is lost, yet not forgotten.*  
> *Look at him now, look what you have done, Luigi.*

The ghostly chorus vanished like smoke. Behind the shelves Wario sagged against the wood, pulling out the worn parchment of [[prop:prop_archive_hall_haunting_docket|the Contract of Accord]] to squint at it in the lantern spill. **"That was the third haunting this week,"** he muttered bitterly when Mr. T whispered that the man looked familiar. **"First Boo's ghost, then that giant moth thing from last week... Now THIS? I'm starting to think the Archive Hall has a grudge against Wario's Enterprise."**

Then the figure in green walked slowly back across the threshold, humming softly under his breath as the memories of Mario trapped behind **King Boo's** chasm closed over him:

> *How can I call myself a hero?*  
> *When I couldn't even save the one — my big bro.*

Clenching a live, glowing **Fire Flower** between both hands, his face drooping and his eyes barely open beneath the cap brim, Beta Luigi shuffled straight toward Wario:

> *Lost his life, I face, so why strife, so why still loom?*  
> *He's already lost to his doom.*

**"What the hell are you doing?!"** Wario blurted, jabbing a finger at his chest. **"You look like death warmed over! I don't need another person falling apart on me right now, Luigi! Maybe this whole Feywild breach was a mistake that's going to cost us everything — so are you going to stand there holding flowers like some kind of funeral bouquet, or tell me what's going on?!"**

Pale apparitions drifted closer around the green overalls, searching for red that was nowhere in the room. Without answering a word, Beta Luigi plucked the working Fire Flower, dropped it onto the wet stones, and **crushed it flat beneath his boot**.

*WAH! A LIVE FIRE FLOWER! Working petals, actual heat still in the stem, stepped on like a cigarette butt in a gutter! I pulled my pen straight out of my coat before my brain caught up with my arm — do you have ANY idea what a live flower goes for on the open market?!*
sections.waluigi_note: Wario blurted two things in panic that belong underlined in red: 'the third haunting this week' and 'this whole Feywild breach.' Neither one slipped out by accident.

sections.name: VI. 'Alone': The Crimson Phantom and the Voice in Italian
sections.imageCaption: A fifteen-foot crimson phantom towers over weeping Beta Luigi on the Archive Hall stones while Mario's faint apparition answers from the mist and a ghostly wall holds Wario and Waluigi back.
sections.overview:
**"WHAT THE— Don't you DARE!"** Waluigi lurched out with his pen shaking in his fist. **"That was a perfect flower! A WORKING flower with actual power and you just CRUSHED IT!"**

Beta Luigi raised his head without looking at either of them, the cap brim still hiding his eyes as he broke open into tears:

> *I'm trying, bro, I swear I'm trying!*  
> *Oh Mario, I'm sorry, there's no use defying!*  
> *The guilt in my heart tears me apart!*  
> *Why'd you depart?!*  
> *All I've ever wanted was to restart!*

Waluigi went white to the lips and slammed both palms against the bookcase hard enough to knock his own cap onto the stones. **"Brother! Do NOT stand there weeping about Mario! You think King Boo cared about your feelings when he trapped him?!"**

Ghosts surged forward between them like an unseen wall, throwing Wario stumble- footed backward when he tried to grab Beta Luigi's shoulders. Beneath the cap, dreadful dark bags hung under Beta Luigi's eyes as he stared through the barrier:

> *You were my number one, bro — now the guilt takes number two whole!*  
> *My cowardice cost your life, yet you can't move on to the afterlife!*  
> *Oh Mario, oh Mario, where did you go?*  
> *I am sorry, bro, you must be so lost and alone.*  
> *After all the wasted years, I still can't face my own fears —*  
> *now I stay sitting here, forced to wipe my own tears.*

A loud crash echoed somewhere in the lower vaults. Then the temperature dropped and **a giant angry crimson ghost** rose fifteen feet into the vault — arms thick as tree trunks, skin burning red — as Beta Luigi crumpled beneath it:

> *This was my only chance, the only time I saw the ball in my court,*  
> *and yet I missed the shot even with all of his support...*  
> *Oh what a failure I have become, how could I let someone down so wholesome.*  
>   
> *YOU WERE THEIR EVERYTHING, THE HAPPINESS YOU'D BRING TO THE LAND —*  
> *NOW ALL OF YOUR BLOOD IS ON MY HANDS.*  
> *OH. GOD. NO.*  
> *Why did I let you go? Please come back home.*

Wario crossed his arms with dead-eyed stubbornness, raising his ledger chart between himself and the crimson giant while the spectral ring closed tighter from every aisle:

> *He would always tell me there is another tomorrow!*  
> *I cannot see! I cannot breathe — I'm suffocating.*  
> *I hear their calls, I hear them all, the ghosts are waiting.*  
> *I face the wrath of reality — my brother is never gonna come back home to me.*

Waluigi's knees gave way on the cold stone floor. His scorched notebook fell open across the flags — pages on *"spectral barriers"* and *"quantum entanglement"* fluttering around his boots — as tears cut clean tracks through the soot on his face. **"Brother! BROTHER! I'm sorry! I'm SO sorry!"**

Beta Luigi whispered on through the closing dark:

> *No matter how much I try to restore it, no matter how much I pray for it,*  
> *life will never be the same without him — life lost to a fate so grim.*  
> *I left in the final hour — why did Luigi sit and cower?!*  
> *Couldn't face the fear of the ghost, left when he needed me the most!*  
> *What kind of brother am I, who would leave their bro to die?*  
> *I am simply not worthy, a hero for sure not me —*  
> *wish I was home back in bed, I hear his voice in my head.*

Then another voice answered — faint at first, unmistakable, coming from nowhere in the stone hall:

> **Mario's voice:** *"Luigi, where did you go? I'm stranded, lost and alone."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"Oh, Mario, where do I go? The kingdom's lost and alone."*  
>   
> **Mario's voice** *(clearer now)*: *"Luigi, where did you go? Ti perdono. Vai avanti."*  
> **Beta Luigi** *(sobbing harder)*: *"Oh... Mario... I TRY, BUT I JUST CAN'T MOVE ON!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Tocca a te salvarli."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"WASN'T READY — STILL HAD MUCH TO IMPROVE ON!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"We still had so much left to do—"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"Mostra loro che sei il fratello..."*  
> **Beta Luigi:** *"—still had so much to prove to you!"*  
>   
> **Mario's voice:** *"...di Mario! Sei Luigi!"*

Every ghost in the Archive Hall went silent at once. Beta Luigi dropped to the stone floor. For three breaths nothing moved except the ceiling drip. Then he murmured into the flags:

> *Every last story has its end, no matter how much I try to pretend.*  
> *Now Luigi's fate left unknown — they laugh at me, but I'll make them atone,*  
> *and this time I'll be sure to do it alone.*

Beta Luigi pushed himself upright, **reached onto the nearest Archive Hall shelf, pulled down a single bound book**, and walked straight out the door alone.
sections.waluigi_note: For the record's translation line: 'Ti perdono. Vai avanti' — I forgive you, go on. 'Tocca a te salvarli' — it is up to you to save them. 'Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano' — Mario is no more, do not let me die in vain. 'Mostra loro che sei il fratello di Mario! Sei Luigi!' — show them you are Mario's brother; you are Luigi. And then he walked out with physical paper under his arm.

sections.name: VII. 'Gold Doesn't Bring Dead People Back': The Corridor and the Feywild Contract
sections.imageCaption: Outside in the dim stone corridor, Wario scars the plaster with his fist and thrusts the worn Contract of Accord at a speechless Mr. T.
sections.overview:
Waluigi stared at the empty doorway with his worn grimoire pressed tight against his chest. **"Sometimes you don't get second chances because there weren't any first chances to begin with,"** he said flatly, walking to the threshold without looking back. **"And this time when Luigi tries to do something heroic, he's going to have to do it alone."**

Inside the quiet hall, **Mr. T** turned to Wario: **"He said Mario, right? That means the Mario disappearance case — it was a side thing, I know, but Wario, think of the gold we can get if we bring Mario back!"**

Wario stared at the empty doorway for three full seconds before his head snapped sideways.

**"Gold?"** His voice came out razored. **"You think I care about gold right now?"** He yanked the **Contract of Accord** out of his coat pocket so hard the worn parchment cracked under his grip, jabbed a finger into Mr. T's chest, and when Mr. T muttered in shock that *Wario not caring about gold meant this must be serious*, drove his fist straight into the stone wall hard enough to scar the plaster.

**"Enough!"** Wario's voice cracked open. **"Mario's gone and I'm standing here talking about bringing him back like some kind of miracle worker?! I don't care if there's gold involved, Mr. T! Gold doesn't bring dead people back!"**

He burst out of the Archive Hall into the dimly lit corridor with Mr. T trailing behind him in stunned silence. **"Get moving! And Mr. T? You're coming with us whether you like it or not! I don't care about your debts, I don't care about Waluigi's gambling problems, and I sure as hell don't care about whatever skeletons are rattling around in Luigi's closet right now! What matters is fixing this before more people get hurt. Before someone else dies because we couldn't do our jobs properly."**

**"What is that book — the Contract of Accord?"** Mr. T asked at his heels.

Wario spun dead in his tracks, white-knuckled fingers crushing the bent corners and torn edges of the parchment between them.

**"This isn't a book. It's a contract. And right now it's the only thing keeping me from walking away from all of this because I know damn well that if I don't fix this somehow, there won't be any coming back — not for anyone. So either you start explaining what goes on in these Feywild contracts or you can just turn around and get out of my way. Because I've got better things to do than stand here arguing about paperwork with a courier who knows too much about gambling debts."**

*WAH! Read that sentence twice and carve it into granite: WARIO SAID HE DOES NOT CARE ABOUT GOLD. In front of a witness! Sober! While holding a Feywild contract by its torn corners! Either the sky is coming down before Darkmoon or the fat man finally read the penalty clause at the bottom!*
sections.waluigi_note: He called it 'these Feywild contracts' to Mr. T's face in the corridor, after calling the sixty-thirty sheet 'the Contract of Accord' at my outpost the night before. Either Wario carries two contracts under one name or the paper in his coat is older and uglier than he told me on the balcony.

aftermath:
Three doors closed on different people within five minutes: Beta Luigi went out first with an unidentified volume off the Archive Hall shelves; Waluigi walked out second with a scorched notebook and three worn grimoire pages; Wario stormed out third with *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise*, a brass cabinet key, the worn Contract of Accord, and Mr. T drafted behind him into the clinic corridor.

Behind them, the Archive Hall remains unguarded, leaking clean rainwater through an uncracked stone ceiling over a crushed Fire Flower, red ink stains, and [[prop:prop_wawario_affiliations_sheet|one song sheet with Waluigi's name blacked out]].
waluigiAssessment:
**1. Two songs went into this record and neither gets cut.** The first one — *'Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and Wario Bowser'* — is thirty lines of slander about mustaches and evil clones that accidentally asked the one real question nobody in this kingdom will answer: *how many copies are walking around right now?* Between Promo Mario's studio, GB Mario's gold road, Mr. L in three copies on the street, and Beta Luigi weeping over a crushed Fire Flower inside the stacks, the idiot who wrote that song was closer to the headcount than the Toad ministries.

**2. Somebody inside the building cooked Wario's books — and left the real ones on the shelf.** Column seven against column nine misses by ten thousand gold, a client deposit is stamped two weeks early, and five thousand gold moves out of and back into the **Treasury of Wonders** across thirty days. Mr. T caught it months ago and wrote `AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO` in the bottom-left corner. Wario never read down that far.

**3. Mr. T clears up yesterday's street mystery without even knowing it.** When Paulo looked at Mr. L outside the clinic last night and said *'I didn't know skinny T wore green,'* we had no courier on file with that handle. Tonight Wario stood in the next corridor over and called Mr. T *'a courier who knows too much about gambling debts.'* Same hill, twenty-four hours apart.

**4. Ghosts do not carry bound books out the door.** Phantoms vanish when the thunder stops. Beta Luigi crushed a real flower on real stone and took a real volume off the shelf before walking out alone. Check every gap on that bookcase before morning.

**5. Watch Wario's coat pocket.** A man who screams *'Gold doesn't bring dead people back!'* and asks a courier how **Feywild contracts** work is not protecting a sixty-thirty publishing split. He is terrified of what happens if defaults trigger.

summary: Continuing directly from the Archive Hall, Wario and Mr. T carry the Contract of Accord into the next leg of the Mario search, and the party travels through the Feywild to a sinister, unnamed house. Waluigi cannot establish whether Mario is inside; Wario argues for an explosive entry while Waluigi and the others dispute the plan and even what to call the group. description:
The corridor argument did not end at the Archive Hall door. Wario kept the worn Contract of Accord with him, and Mr. T went along as the group continued the search that Wario had said mattered more than the gold. Their route carried them into the Feywild. The transcript gives no travel interval, no hour, and no reading from the Feyward pocket clock; the date is therefore chained to the Material-clock corridor scene immediately before it, without pretending the transition had a measured duration.

They eventually reached a house that looked wrong even by Feywild standards: dark, ominous, and isolated enough to make the group stop and argue before trying the entrance. Waluigi consulted his grimoire and floated the name “Feywild Cavern of Despair,” but that is his description, not a verified place-name. He suspected the house might be connected to Mario’s disappearance, yet nobody had seen Mario there. His presence inside remained a possibility, not a discovery.

The locked entrance turned the rescue into a dispute over method. Wario pressed for explosives; Waluigi objected and pushed for a less destructive way in. Jory Dobbs and Mr. T were part of the discussion as the group weighed the risk, the lock, and who should take the next action. Waluigi tried to work the problem with his grimoire while the argument kept circling back to Wario’s preferred solution. Nobody established that an explosive had been used.

The argument expanded from the door to the group itself: Wario tried to frame the search as a party, and the companions traded possible names. Waluigi had opinions, naturally, but the transcript does not establish a settled name for the group. The talk did not make the house any less ominous or prove that the missing Mario was inside.

At the threshold, Beta Luigi was revealed as the figure connected to the door. The scene records him speaking to himself and then engaging with the others. Wario challenged him to act with courage; Beta Luigi acknowledged that he wanted to help rescue Mario but did not feel brave. Wario urged him to come with them. The transcript also uses “Luigi” in a way that is not fully reconciled with its explicit identification of Beta Luigi, so this record does not infer a second identity or silently resolve the wording.

The door finally opened, but the account does not settle exactly whose action released it: Waluigi reports a click during the attempt, while the final beat identifies Beta Luigi opening the door. The group reaches the threshold. The record stops there. No interior search is described, Mario is not located, and nothing beyond the doorway is confirmed.
outcome: Filed as an open lead in the ongoing Mario search. The party reaches an unnamed house in the Feywild; the entrance opens and Beta Luigi is at the threshold. The transcript does not confirm that Mario is in the house, show anyone searching inside, or establish what lies past the doorway. The exact mechanism that opened the door is also unresolved.

waluigiAssessment:
1. Wario leaves the Archive Hall saying gold does not bring dead people back, then brings a contract with him and proposes explosives at the first locked door. I am not calling that a contradiction until I see the clause. I am calling it a pattern.

2. “Mario may be in there” is a lead, not a location. A dark house, a spooky grimoire label, and Wario’s confidence do not add up to a witness. Nobody sees Mario. Nobody says they have searched the rooms.

3. The group argued about what to call itself before it had even crossed the threshold. I would like the archive to record that the name remains unsettled, so no one can later claim I approved a title I was still improving.

4. Beta Luigi admits he wants to help and is afraid. That is more useful than pretending the fear is not there. Wario can push; the door still has to open.

5. The door does open. Who opened it, exactly, is less clear than the people outside would like. The record ends at the threshold. I refuse to let anybody turn an open door into a successful rescue by grammatical optimism.

sections.name: I. The Contract Leaves the Archive Hall
sections.overview: Wario and Mr. T continue from the corridor with the Contract of Accord as the search for Mario resumes. Their route takes them into the Feywild; the record supplies no travel duration or local clock reading.

sections.name: II. A House with No Verified Name
sections.overview: The group reaches a sinister, unnamed house. Waluigi’s grimoire description, “Feywild Cavern of Despair,” is preserved as his guess, not a confirmed place-name. No one has evidence that Mario is inside.

sections.name: III. The Argument at the Locked Door
sections.overview: Wario advocates an explosive entry. Waluigi objects and considers other ways through the lock; Jory Dobbs and Mr. T are part of the group’s discussion. The transcript does not establish that an explosive is used.

sections.name: IV. A Party Before an Entry
sections.overview: The companions also argue over what to call the group. Waluigi contests the suggestions, but no final or official party name is established in the record.

sections.name: V. Beta Luigi at the Threshold
sections.overview: Beta Luigi appears in connection with the doorway, speaks to the others, and admits that he wants to help rescue Mario but is afraid. Wario urges him to come. The transcript’s separate uses of “Luigi” are not reconciled here.

sections.name: VI. The Door Opens; the Search Does Not Resolve
sections.overview: The entrance opens. The transcript mentions a click during the attempt and identifies Beta Luigi in the final opening beat, but does not settle the exact mechanism. The record ends at the threshold; Mario and the house’s interior remain unseen.
